items.title: Lawrence Cotton Interview, 1996-12-10
items.q: they called him Summer Ross, and he could play, man

ctx.x: I think he was 68 when he died. Okay, well then he was a little older than tuts, a bit older than tuts.

Yeah. But he comes out of that same, that same period, yeah. Same period, same thing? Yeah, because I had another uncle, Uncle Tat, his brother, they called him Summer Ross, and he could play, man. They had several guys around there, man, those guys could play, man. And when you heard them you had to sit down and listen. Whatever you were doing you just sit down and take note of what's going on. Oh yeah. Oh yeah. Yeah. Yeah, like Walter Lewis, man. Walter, about in his eighties, man. And Walter as quiet as Walter…

I've never heard him play blues. He's always played more, I don't know, supper music. Whenever I hear him, I'm going, wait a minute, man. Can we do something a little more raunchy? Come on. Yeah. And he's always in a situation where he's got to play. Yeah. Like, you know, he's got to play to the audience, so to speak.
